summary: Anthropic researchers introduce CHIVE, an agentic pipeline that discovers unexpected LLM behaviors and tests explanations via counterfactual prompt edits, finding that current activation-reading interpretability tools provide no predictive uplift over reading transcripts alone.

practices.reason: Provides a method (counterfactual simulatability via automated prompt-edit experiments) for evaluating whether an explanation or interpretability tool actually predicts model behavior, which a team could use to test its own interpretability claims.
practices.quote: we evaluate explanations through the lens of counterfactual simulatability : a good explanation of a behavior should help you predict what the model will do on related counterfactual inputs.

practices.reason: Describes an agentic pipeline architecture (screening, investigator agent, predictor agent) for automated behavior discovery, though not directly reusable without more detail on implementation.
practices.quote: We introduce CHIVE (Counterfactual Hypothesis Investigation Via Edits), an agentic pipeline that generates such data automatically.
